# ECN-2026-016 - Change notice - Machining shot blast cabinet #1
Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01

Reason for change
- Background: During the P3-L3 machining process audit (see SB-1010) and subsequent corrective maintenance reviews, maintenance staff identified recurring lubricant compatibility issues in the shot blast cabinet drive and pivot assemblies on EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Inspection records indicate increased deposition in splash shields and premature buildup on exposed bearings affecting access and cleaning efficiency. The current preventive maintenance approach did not fully address residue characteristics or handling records.
- Purpose: Standardize the lubricant for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) to a single approved part and update routines, work instructions, and records to reduce residue buildup, simplify procurement, and ensure consistent maintenance execution across line P3-L3. The lubricant part number for Machining shot blast cabinet #1 (EQ-P3-L3-SB01) is CFW-LUB-709.
- Rationale: Using a defined, approved lubricant removes ambiguity from maintenance steps in SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04, improves traceability of consumables, and aligns with material control objectives in SB-1010. The selected part has been evaluated by maintenance engineering for compatibility with cabinet materials and containment methods; field trials on a sister unit showed reduced tenacity of deposited residues and easier removal during scheduled cleaning.

Affected items
- Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01 (Machining shot blast cabinet #1) — all lubrication points identified in existing schematics and SOPs for this unit.
- Documents and procedures:
  - SOP-P3-L3-03 (weekly and monthly lubrication and cabinet inspection tasks) — updated to specify CFW-LUB-709 at each lubrication step and to add handling notes.
  - SOP-P3-L3-04 (cabinet cleaning and abrasive handling) — updated to include post-lubrication residue checks and disposal/kitting requirements.
  - SB-1010 (equipment specification and audit checklist) — cross-reference table to be updated to show CFW-LUB-709 as the specified lubricant for EQ-P3-L3-SB01.
- Parts and storeroom: Parts catalog entry for EQ-P3-L3-SB01 maintenance kit; stock record to include CFW-LUB-709 as the designated lubricant for this cabinet.
- Training: Maintenance technicians assigned to P3-L3 and operators interfacing with EQ-P3-L3-SB01 who perform minor maintenance will require training on the updated SOPs and handling precautions related to CFW-LUB-709.

Implementation
- Effective date: Implementation of the change will begin on the date of approval by the signatories in the Approvals section and will be phased into routine maintenance per the steps below.
- Steps:
  1. Documentation updates: Revise SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04 to include explicit call-outs for CFW-LUB-709 and updated work-step notes. Revise SB-1010 cross-reference table. Issue redline and controlled copies.
  2. Parts provisioning: Create a stocked item entry for CFW-LUB-709 in the P3 storeroom and add to the preventive maintenance kit contents for EQ-P3-L3-SB01. Tag current lubricant stock to be used only after confirmation of compatibility or returned to vendor.
  3. Pilot application: Perform a controlled application of CFW-LUB-709 on EQ-P3-L3-SB01 during a scheduled maintenance window. Document pre- and post-application condition with photos and checklist items from SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04.
  4. Verification and acceptance: Maintenance engineering to review pilot records and, if acceptable, sign off to proceed with full roll-out.
  5. Full roll-out: Replace ad hoc lubricants in the cabinet with CFW-LUB-709 during the next scheduled maintenance tasks, following updated SOP steps.
- Work-step examples to be added to SOPs:
  - Example 1: Apply CFW-LUB-709 to the outer pivot pin using a clean dispenser until shop-recommended indication (see SOP-P3-L3-03 for dispenser handling). Wipe excess and inspect splash shield per SOP-P3-L3-04 checklist.
  - Example 2: After cabinet cleaning, record lubricant lot and dispenser ID in the maintenance log entry for traceability.
- Records to keep:
  - Maintenance log entries on the EQ-P3-L3-SB01 equipment history: technician name, date, lot number of CFW-LUB-709, dispenser ID, observations pre/post-application, and link to photo records.
  - Pilot trial report and acceptance sign-off retained in the equipment file.
  - Updated SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04 controlled copies and redline histories.
  - Storeroom transaction logs showing receipt and issue of CFW-LUB-709 for EQ-P3-L3-SB01.
  - Audit trail in SB-1010 showing the change and sign-off for traceability.
- Safety and environmental notes: Add handling and spill containment steps for CFW-LUB-709 to SOP-P3-L3-04. Ensure Material Safety Data Sheet for CFW-LUB-709 is filed with plant safety and referenced in the updated SOPs.

Approvals
- Review path: Maintenance Engineering → Process Engineering → Quality Assurance → Plant Management.
- Required approval elements:
  - Confirmation that CFW-LUB-709 is stocked and traceable in the P3 storeroom.
  - Sign-off on updated SOP-P3-L3-03 and SOP-P3-L3-04 controlled copies.
  - Entry in SB-1010 noting the change and linking to the revised SOPs.
- Approval sign-off block (to be completed by approvers):
  - Maintenance Engineering: name / signature / date
  - Process Engineering: name / signature / date
  - Quality Assurance: name / signature / date
  - Plant Management: name / signature / date

Related documents
- SB-1010
- SOP-P3-L3-03
- SOP-P3-L3-04

Change control notes
- Revision: Rev C applies to this document; record the revision in the ECN log and attach redline to the prior revision.
- Rollback: If field performance of CFW-LUB-709 is unsatisfactory during pilot or roll-out, revert to prior lubricant only after documented QA concurrence and disposal or quarantine of CFW-LUB-709 stock as required. All deviations to be recorded against the ECN number.
- Post-implementation review: Schedule a 30-day field review after full roll-out to assess residue characteristics, cleaning time impact, and record completeness; capture findings in the equipment history under ECN-2026-016.
